Analysis of a body on the basis of reflectance,
absorptance, and transmittance:
a. For a body if t = 0 then, r + a = 1. Therefore for ‘a’ to be greater r must be smaller and
vice versa. This means good reflectors are bad absorbers and vice-versa.
b. For a body if t = 0 and r = 0 then, a = 1. That is, if a body absorbs all the radiant energy
falling on it, neither it reflects nor it transmits it. As a result, a body appears black. In this
situation, the given body is known as a black body. Not in all cases the black body appears
black. For example, the sun behaves as a black body but does not appear black.

Explain. 12.9 Black Body and Black Body Radiation A perfectly black body is an idealized physical body that absorbs all incidents of heat radiation, regardless of wavelengths or angle of incidence. Also, a perfectly black body emits radiations of all possible wavelengths when heated. For a perfect black body, the value of absorptance is unity, and that of emissivity is also unity. A good absorber is a good emitter. The sun emits radiations of all wavelengths. So, it can be considered as a black body. A black body is a good emitter so that it can emit radiation of all possible wavelengths. A perfectly black body cannot absorb all the radiant energy but neither it reflects nor it transmits. Hence a perfect body appears black at room temperature and is known as a black body. However, at higher temperatures, it can actually glow at visible wavelengths. Therefore, the term 'black body' is also referred to an object that glows. For example; the sun. Black body radiation is given off not only by extremely hot objects but also by anything which is above the absolute zero temperature. From stars to ice cubes, they may give black body radiation. A perfectly black body cannot be realized in actual practice. The nearest approach to a perfect black body is a surface coated with lamp black or platinum black. Such a surface absorbs 96% to 98% of the incident radiation. Ferry's black body is an example of perfect black body realized in practice.
Emissive Power Emissive power is defined as the rate of heat radiation radiated by a unit area of a body at a particular temperature. It is denoted by E. Mathematically.
